section: World Trade Organization - structure, agreements (AoA, TRIPS, TRIMS, GATS), dispute settlement, India's issues
subsections: Structure - Ministerial Conference, General Council, DSB, TPRB
Agreement on Agriculture - boxes, de minimis, Peace Clause, PSH
TRIPS - compulsory licensing, Doha Declaration, COVID waiver, GI
Dispute settlement - Appellate Body crisis, India's disputes

accepted.s: The World Trade Organization was established on 1 January 1995 under which agreement?
o: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade
accepted.x: The WTO was established on 1 January 1995 under the Marrakesh Agreement after the Uruguay Round.
accepted.tq: Use the founding agreement and date as the identifying pair.
accepted.sec: WTO - establishment, predecessor, HQ, membership

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between GATT and the WTO?
o: The WTO deals only with goods, whereas GATT deals with services and intellectual property.
The WTO replaced the GATT system, while GATT survived as an integral WTO agreement.
GATT replaced the WTO after the Uruguay Round.
GATT and the WTO are completely unrelated institutions.
accepted.x: The WTO replaced the GATT 1947/48 system, but GATT continues as an integral WTO agreement.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between an institutional predecessor and an agreement retained within the successor framework.
accepted.sec: WTO - establishment, predecessor, HQ, membership

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the WTO:
1. Its decision-making is based on consensus.
2. It follows the principle of one-country-one-vote.
3. Its governance covers goods, services and intellectual property.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The WTO uses consensus-based, one-country-one-vote decision-making and covers goods, services and intellectual property.
accepted.tq: Combine institutional principles with the WTO’s expanded subject coverage.
accepted.sec: WTO - establishment, predecessor, HQ, membership

accepted.s: As of March 2026, the membership of the World Trade Organization is:
accepted.x: The WTO has 166 members as of March 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the latest figure from the older membership figure of 164.
accepted.sec: WTO - establishment, predecessor, HQ, membership

accepted.s: Which pair was admitted as the latest members of the WTO in 2024?
accepted.x: Comoros and Timor-Leste became the latest WTO members in 2024.
accepted.tq: Match the latest membership fact rather than the older accession examples.
accepted.sec: WTO - establishment, predecessor, HQ, membership

accepted.s: Which WTO body is the highest decision-making body and is required to meet at least once every two years?
accepted.x: The Ministerial Conference is the WTO’s highest decision-making body and must meet at least once every two years.
accepted.tq: Identify the highest authority by its formal meeting requirement.
accepted.sec: Structure - Ministerial Conference, General Council, DSB, TPRB

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (WTO body)
A. General Council
B. Dispute Settlement Body
C. Trade Policy Review Body
D. Ministerial Conference

List-II (Function)
1. Periodic review of members’ trade policies
2. Highest decision-making body
3. Operates between Ministerial Conferences
4. Deals with panels and Appellate Body rulings

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The General Council runs the WTO between Ministerial Conferences; the DSB handles dispute rulings; the TPRB reviews trade policies; and the Ministerial Conference is the highest decision-making body.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair of each body with its distinctive function.
accepted.sec: Structure - Ministerial Conference, General Council, DSB, TPRB

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Dispute Settlement Body — Panels and Appellate Body rulings
Trade Policy Review Body — Periodic review of members’ trade policies
Ministerial Conference — Investigation of anti-dumping cases in India
Council for Trade in Goods — Oversight of GATT
accepted.x: The Ministerial Conference is the WTO’s highest decision-making body; investigation of anti-dumping cases in India is not its function.
accepted.tq: Find the body-function mismatch by separating WTO governance from domestic investigation.
accepted.sec: Structure - Ministerial Conference, General Council, DSB, TPRB

accepted.s:
Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the WTO Ministerial Conferences and events?
A. Singapore Ministerial Conference
B. Seattle Ministerial Conference
C. Cancún Ministerial Conference
D. MC12 at Geneva
E. MC13 at Abu Dhabi
accepted.x: The sequence is Singapore in 1996, Seattle in 1999, Cancún in 2003, Geneva in 2022 and Abu Dhabi in 2024.
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last events, then place the intermediate conferences by year.
accepted.sec: Structure - Ministerial Conference, General Council, DSB, TPRB

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The first WTO Ministerial Conference was held at Singapore in 1996. Seattle was in 1999, Cancún in 2003 and MC12 was held at Geneva in 2022.
accepted.tq: Use date-location discrimination among closely related Ministerial Conferences.
accepted.sec: Structure - Ministerial Conference, General Council, DSB, TPRB

accepted.s: Which WTO Ministerial Conferences are specifically associated with a breakdown of negotiations?
accepted.x: The Seattle Ministerial Conference of 1999 and the Cancún Ministerial Conference of 2003 broke down.
accepted.tq: Separate failed negotiating conferences from conferences identified mainly by their locations or dates.
accepted.sec: Structure - Ministerial Conference, General Council, DSB, TPRB

accepted.s: The Council for Trade in Goods oversees which agreement, and which committees are associated with it?
o: GATS; banking, insurance and tourism committees
GATT; agriculture, market access, TBT and SPS committees
TRIPS; patents, copyright and trademarks committees
TRIMS; investment, taxation and exchange-control committees
accepted.x: The Council for Trade in Goods oversees GATT and includes committees dealing with agriculture, market access, TBT and SPS.
accepted.tq: Link the council to its principal agreement and its listed committees.
accepted.sec: Structure - Ministerial Conference, General Council, DSB, TPRB

accepted.s:
Match the following WTO agreements with their principal subjects:

A. AoA
B. SPS
C. TBT
D. GATS

1. Trade in services
2. Food safety and animal and plant health
3. Agricultural market access, domestic support and export subsidies
4. Technical regulations and standards

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: AoA concerns agriculture; SPS concerns food, animal and plant health; TBT concerns technical regulations and standards; and GATS concerns services.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive subject of each agreement and eliminate crossed codes.
accepted.sec: Agreements → subject

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Anti-dumping — Duties on goods sold below normal value
TRIPS — Minimum standards for all forms of intellectual property rights
TRIMS — Investment measures that distort trade
GATS — Subsidies that are prohibited, actionable and non-actionable
accepted.x: GATS deals with trade in services. The classification of subsidies as prohibited, actionable and non-actionable belongs to the SCM Agreement.
accepted.tq: Detect the agreement-subject swap among neighbouring WTO agreements.
accepted.sec: Agreements → subject

accepted.s: Under the SCM Agreement, which of the following categories of subsidies are recognised?
accepted.x: The SCM Agreement identifies prohibited, actionable or countervailable, and non-actionable subsidies, including certain R&D, regional and environmental subsidies.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the SCM subsidy classification from the agricultural box classification.
accepted.sec: Agreements → subject

accepted.s: In India, which body handles anti-dumping, countervailing and safeguard investigations under WTO rules?
accepted.x: The Directorate General of Trade Remedies handles anti-dumping, countervailing and safeguard investigations in India.
accepted.tq: Ask which domestic authority performs the specified trade-remedy function.
accepted.sec: Agreements → subject

accepted.s: Which two agreements are identified as the only new WTO agreements concluded in the first 30 years of the organisation?
o: Trade Facilitation Agreement and Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
accepted.x: The Trade Facilitation Agreement and the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies are identified as the only new WTO agreements in that period.
accepted.tq: Use the word “only” carefully to identify the complete pair rather than older Uruguay Round agreements.
accepted.sec: Agreements → subject

accepted.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched with the WTO’s agricultural support boxes?

1. Green Box — support regarded as non-trade-distorting and having no limit
2. Blue Box — direct payments that limit production
3. Amber Box — measures such as output-linked MSP and input subsidies subject to reduction commitments
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Green Box support has no reduction limit, Blue Box payments are linked to production-limiting conditions, and Amber Box measures are subject to reduction commitments.
accepted.tq: Separate the three agricultural boxes by both content and regulatory treatment.
accepted.sec: Agreement on Agriculture - boxes, de minimis, Peace Clause, PSH

accepted.s: Which one of the following is an example of Green Box support under the Agreement on Agriculture?
o: Minimum Support Price linked to production
Input subsidy on fertiliser tied to output
accepted.x: Research and disease control are Green Box measures, along with infrastructure, food security and decoupled income support.
accepted.tq: Classify the policy by checking whether it is decoupled and non-trade-distorting.
accepted.sec: Agreement on Agriculture - boxes, de minimis, Peace Clause, PSH

accepted.s: Which of the following is included in the Amber Box under the Agreement on Agriculture?
o: Input subsidies for power, fertiliser, seeds and irrigation tied to output
accepted.x: Amber Box measures include MSP and output-linked input subsidies such as power, fertiliser, seeds and irrigation, and are subject to reduction commitments.
accepted.tq: Identify the output-linked support rather than exempt Green Box measures.
accepted.sec: Agreement on Agriculture - boxes, de minimis, Peace Clause, PSH

accepted.s: The de minimis limit for agricultural domestic support is what percentage of production value for developed and developing countries, respectively?
accepted.x: The de minimis limit is 5% of production value for developed countries and 10% for developing countries.
accepted.tq: Read the paired percentages in the correct developed-country/developing-country order.
accepted.sec: Agreement on Agriculture - boxes, de minimis, Peace Clause, PSH

accepted.s: The Peace Clause adopted at Bali in 2013 provides protection to developing countries from disputes concerning:
o: Trade in banking and insurance services
accepted.x: The Bali Peace Clause shields developing-country public stockholding programmes from disputes until a permanent solution is found.
accepted.tq: Link the clause to its conference, year and specific agricultural issue.
accepted.sec: Agreement on Agriculture - boxes, de minimis, Peace Clause, PSH

accepted.s: Which country first invoked the WTO Peace Clause for rice in 2020?
accepted.x: India was the first country to invoke the Peace Clause for rice in 2020.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the invoking country from countries associated with India’s sugar dispute.
accepted.sec: Agreement on Agriculture - boxes, de minimis, Peace Clause, PSH

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding public stockholding at MC14 in 2026:
1. No permanent solution was reached on public stockholding.
2. India and the African Group sought a permanent shield for programmes such as the NFSA.
3. The issue was declared permanently settled at MC14.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. MC14 did not produce a permanent solution; India and the African Group continued to seek a permanent shield for programmes such as the NFSA.
accepted.tq: Reject the extreme finality of “permanently settled” when the issue remains unresolved.
accepted.sec: Agreement on Agriculture - boxes, de minimis, Peace Clause, PSH

accepted.s: India amended the Patents Act in 2005 primarily to comply with:
accepted.x: India amended the Patents Act in 2005 to bring its patent regime into compliance with TRIPS minimum intellectual-property standards.
accepted.tq: Match the domestic legislative change with the relevant WTO agreement.
accepted.sec: TRIPS - compulsory licensing, Doha Declaration, COVID waiver, GI

accepted.s: The Doha Declaration on TRIPS and public health affirmed that TRIPS:
o: Prevents members from regulating medicines in public interest
Must not stop members from protecting public health
Eliminates compulsory licensing by developing countries
accepted.x: The Doha Declaration of 2001 affirmed that TRIPS must not prevent members from taking measures to protect public health.
accepted.tq: Test the public-health flexibility principle against restrictive distractors.
accepted.sec: TRIPS - compulsory licensing, Doha Declaration, COVID waiver, GI

accepted.s: Which provision and mechanism were used by India to address public-health concerns under the TRIPS framework?
accepted.x: India used Section 3(d) of the Patents Act against evergreening and compulsory licensing as TRIPS flexibilities.
accepted.tq: Identify the domestic legal tools associated with the international flexibility.
accepted.sec: TRIPS - compulsory licensing, Doha Declaration, COVID waiver, GI

accepted.s: India’s first compulsory licence was granted in 2012 in the Natco-Bayer case. It concerned:
accepted.x: India’s first compulsory licence was the Natco-Bayer case in 2012 and concerned a pharmaceutical patent.
accepted.tq: Use the parties and year to identify the subject of the compulsory licence.
accepted.sec: TRIPS - compulsory licensing, Doha Declaration, COVID waiver, GI

accepted.s: Which countries jointly proposed the COVID-related TRIPS waiver in 2020?
accepted.x: India and South Africa jointly proposed the COVID-related TRIPS waiver in 2020.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the proposal sponsors from countries involved in WTO disputes.
accepted.sec: TRIPS - compulsory licensing, Doha Declaration, COVID waiver, GI

accepted.s: What was the nature of the TRIPS waiver adopted at MC12 in 2022?
o: A limited waiver for vaccine patents
A waiver restricted exclusively to geographical indications
A permanent waiver for all intellectual-property rights
A complete abolition of all pharmaceutical patents
accepted.x: MC12 adopted a limited waiver relating to vaccine patents; it did not abolish all pharmaceutical or intellectual-property patents.
accepted.tq: Watch the scope qualifier “limited” and avoid expanding a partial waiver into a general one.
accepted.sec: TRIPS - compulsory licensing, Doha Declaration, COVID waiver, GI

accepted.s: The Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act was enacted in India in 1999 mainly to meet obligations under:
accepted.x: India enacted the Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999 to meet TRIPS obligations.
accepted.tq: Match the Indian statute with the WTO agreement covering intellectual property.
accepted.sec: TRIPS - compulsory licensing, Doha Declaration, COVID waiver, GI

accepted.s: Which statement regarding India and the Lisbon Agreement/Geneva Act is correct?
o: India joined the Geneva Act before enacting its GI legislation.
India is not a member of the Lisbon Agreement or the Geneva Act of 2015.
India is a member only of the Lisbon Agreement.
India is a member of both the Lisbon Agreement and the Geneva Act of 2015.
accepted.x: India is not a member of either the Lisbon Agreement or the Geneva Act of 2015.
accepted.tq: Test the negative membership fact against plausible treaty-accession alternatives.
accepted.sec: TRIPS - compulsory licensing, Doha Declaration, COVID waiver, GI

accepted.s: At MC14, which development occurred in relation to TRIPS non-violation complaints?
o: Non-violation complaints were abolished from the TRIPS Agreement.
The moratorium, in force since 1995, lapsed.
The moratorium was replaced by compulsory licensing.
accepted.x: The moratorium on TRIPS non-violation complaints, which had existed since 1995, lapsed at MC14.
accepted.tq: Use the time marker “since 1995” to distinguish lapse from extension or abolition.
accepted.sec: TRIPS - compulsory licensing, Doha Declaration, COVID waiver, GI

accepted.s: The present crisis in the WTO dispute-settlement system primarily resulted from:
o: The African Group rejecting all panel reports
The General Council refusing to meet between Ministerial Conferences
India withdrawing from the Marrakesh Agreement
The United States blocking appointments to the Appellate Body
accepted.x: The United States blocked Appellate Body appointments, paralysing the WTO’s two-tier dispute-settlement system.
accepted.tq: Identify the actor responsible for the institutional blockage rather than the affected body.
accepted.sec: Dispute settlement - Appellate Body crisis, India's disputes

accepted.s: The BRICS New Delhi Declaration of September 2026 sought:
o: Restoration of the WTO Appellate Body
accepted.x: The BRICS New Delhi Declaration sought restoration of the WTO Appellate Body.
accepted.tq: Match the declaration with its institutional reform objective.
accepted.sec: Dispute settlement - Appellate Body crisis, India's disputes

accepted.s: India’s dispute concerning domestic-content requirements in the Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission was brought by which complainant, and what was the outcome?
accepted.x: The United States challenged India’s domestic-content requirements in the JNNSM solar-panel dispute, and India lost in 2016.
accepted.tq: Pair the complainant, subject and outcome before considering the year.
accepted.sec: Dispute settlement - Appellate Body crisis, India's disputes

accepted.s: Which countries were complainants in the WTO dispute concerning India’s sugar subsidies?
o: United States, Japan and the European Union
accepted.x: Brazil, Australia and Guatemala complained against India’s sugar subsidies. The panel ruled against India in 2021 and India appealed.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the sugar-dispute complainants from those in the ICT-tariff dispute.
accepted.sec: Dispute settlement - Appellate Body crisis, India's disputes

accepted.s: Which group of complainants challenged India’s ICT tariffs, and what was the panel year?
accepted.x: The European Union, Japan and Chinese Taipei challenged India’s ICT tariffs; the panel ruled against India in 2023 and India appealed.
accepted.tq: Use the complainant cluster and year to separate ICT tariffs from other disputes.
accepted.sec: Dispute settlement - Appellate Body crisis, India's disputes

accepted.s: The WTO dispute concerning India’s export subsidy schemes such as MEIS and SEZ schemes was initiated by:
accepted.x: The United States challenged India’s export subsidy schemes, including MEIS and SEZ schemes; the panel ruled against India in 2019 and India appealed.
accepted.tq: Match the challenged scheme with its complainant and panel outcome.
accepted.sec: Dispute settlement - Appellate Body crisis, India's disputes

accepted.s: Why are India’s appeals in the listed WTO disputes described as being “into the void”?
o: The WTO has no dispute panels for trade matters.
The Appellate Body lacks members and cannot function normally.
India has withdrawn its appeals voluntarily.
The complainants refused to submit written arguments.
accepted.x: Because the Appellate Body lacks members, appeals cannot proceed through the normal two-tier system and are described as being “into the void”.
accepted.tq: Apply the institutional-crisis fact to the practical consequence for an appeal.
accepted.sec: Dispute settlement - Appellate Body crisis, India's disputes

accepted.s: India raised the issue of the United Kingdom’s steel safeguard at which WTO body in May 2026?
accepted.x: India raised the UK steel safeguard at the Council for Trade in Goods in May 2026. The issue was an irritant for the India-UK CETA.
accepted.tq: Identify the WTO body from the subject matter and distinguish it from dispute adjudication bodies.
accepted.sec: Structure - Ministerial Conference, General Council, DSB, TPRB

accepted.s: India’s steel exports to the United Kingdom were valued at approximately what amount in 2025–26?
accepted.x: India’s steel exports to the United Kingdom were valued at $893.4 million in 2025–26.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the reported export value from nearby altered figures.
accepted.sec: Structure - Ministerial Conference, General Council, DSB, TPRB
